candidates.attacker_control: The Jiffle script string is normally supplied by the application/remote client: Jiffle.setScript(String) (public API), JiffleBuilder.script(String), and the JAI operation "Jiffle" whose SCRIPT parameter is read in JiffleRIF.create() (paramBlock.getObjectParameter(JiffleDescriptor.SCRIPT_ARG)) before compiling it via Jiffle.compile()/getRuntimeInstance(). Any deployment that compiles user-supplied scripts (e.g. a WPS/rendering process exposing the Jiffle operation, as done in GeoTools/GeoServer) passes attacker-controlled text into this path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that stripComments removes ordinary /*...*/ comments and that numeric literals, identifiers, option values and function names are validated/whitelisted (Double/Integer.valueOf, OptionLookup, FunctionLookup), so the breakout does not rely on those; checked that Janino's SimpleCompiler is the sole compilation step and that the runtime class is loaded via the compiler classloader; checked that createRuntimeSource explicitly refuses script-in-docs (scriptInDocs=true throws) yet still embeds the script for the normal false path, showing the sanitization intent is not enforced; searched for other sinks (no SQL/XML/deserialization/exec/network/path traversal in main code) and considered them weaker.
candidates.impact: Java source/code injection into the runtime class compiled in-process: at minimum attacker-influenced code becomes part of a class loaded by the application; where the injected class is initialized, this yields arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the hosting process (e.g. an application server exposing Jiffle), otherwise it enables integrity compromise of the compiled runtime and potential further classloader abuse. Confidentiality/integrity/availability impact on any service that compiles untrusted Jiffle scripts.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) The attacker can supply or influence a Jiffle script that is compiled by this library (Jiffle API or JAI "Jiffle" operation). 2) The script must parse successfully and contain a '*/' sequence that is not part of a '/* ... */' block comment stripped by stripComments; the most plausible carrier is a '//' line comment, because the helper is explicitly named BLOCK_COMMENT_STRIPPER and line comments are not handled. 3) The generated source is compiled with Janino (SimpleCompiler.cook) and the produced runtime class is loaded/instantiated; execution of injected declarations depends on which injected class gets initialized — immediate RCE could not be proven from source alone.
candidates.root_cause: Jiffle.createRuntimeSource() unconditionally calls writer.setScript(stripComments(theScript)) even when the caller requested no script-in-docs (scriptInDocs=false; the code only throws when scriptInDocs=true). SourceWriter.getScript() is then consumed by Script.write(), which writes every script line into a generated Javadoc block comment (" * " + line). stripComments() only strips "/* ... */" block comments (Jiffle.java BLOCK_COMMENT_STRIPPER); a "*/" sequence remaining in the script (e.g. inside a line comment, if supported by the Jiffle grammar) closes the generated Javadoc early and the remainder of that script line is emitted as raw Java. Since the same source is fed to Janino SimpleCompiler and the resulting class is loaded and instantiated, attacker-controlled Java declarations become part of the compiled runtime class.
candidates.title: Jiffle script text is embedded unsanitized into generated Java source, enabling Java code injection into the compiled runtime class
candidates.trace: Untrusted script (JAI "Jiffle" SCRIPT parameter / Jiffle.setScript) -> Jiffle.compile() parses it -> getRuntimeInstance()/getRuntimeInstance(model) -> createRuntimeInstance(...) -> createRuntimeSource(model, baseClassName, false) -> writer.setScript(stripComments(theScript)); stripComments only deletes /*...*/ blocks -> SourceWriter.getScript() -> Script.write(): lines 94-106 split the script on newline and emit each line into a /** ... */ block comment -> a surviving '*/' in a script line terminates the comment and turns the rest of the line into generated Java (subsequent lines can continue the injected Java because text opened with /* is closed by the generator's own trailing ' */') -> SimpleCompiler.cook(runtimeSource) compiles it -> compiler.getClassLoader().loadClass(runtimeClassName).newInstance() loads/instantiates the class containing the injected declarations.
candidates.unverified: The ANTLR grammar files (src/main/antlr4/*.g4) and Jiffle userguide/.jfl resources are not present in this snapshot, so I could not verify whether '//' line comments are tokenized by the Jiffle lexer (the precondition for a '*/' surviving stripComments). I also could not verify at runtime that injected top-level declarations are initialized/executed by Janino at compile/instantiate time (no code execution permitted); execution likely depends on the injected class being referenced/initialized, while guaranteed effects are injected compiled code and potential classloader/resource impact. No test files or dynamic analysis were available to confirm exploitability.

coverage_summary: Reviewed the 490-file snapshot (415 Java files) using text search plus the P1 relation index. Searched broadly for SQL/JDBC, XML/XXE, deserialization/readObject, command execution/ProcessBuilder/Runtime.exec, network/SSRF, file path/temp-file/upload sinks, Class.forName/newInstance/setAccessible reflection, and crypto/random usage; none of the classic injection categories is present in main code. Focused source review on: the whole jt-jiffle module (Jiffle.java, JiffleBuilder, JiffleRIF/JiffleDescriptor/JiffleOpImage, parser workers and node writers, runtime classes), RegistryFileParser/ConcurrentOperationRegistry wiring, JAIExt/ImageUtilities/PropertyUtil, colorindexer (PackedHistogram/Quantizer), lookup (LookupTableFactory), artifact filter median code, mosaic bean, buffer/zonal index-hint sites, and viewer/demo utilities. The index confirms syntax-only coverage (no control/data flow, no semantic resolution) and names 415 parsed Java files with no omissions; its 'security_call' facts were treated as navigation hints and each inspected hit was verified in source (mostly write()/query() name matches).
limitations: ANTLR grammar files (src/main/antlr4/*.g4), Jiffle .jfl scripts, userguide .rst files and all test sources are absent from the snapshot; the lexer/comment token rules and the exact Jiffle surface syntax could not be verified, which is the key uncertainty for the submitted candidate.
No build, execution, tests or dynamic analysis were performed (not permitted); all conclusions are static, and 'runtime-confirmed' is not claimed.

The P1 index is syntax/navigation only: no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution or reachability proof; coverage of the large image-operator files (e.g. ZonalStatsOpImage, MosaicOpImage, Scale/Scale2/Warp families) was sampled via targeted searches rather than read line-by-line.
Dependency-level issues (e.g. Guava/Janino/ANTLR versions in poms) were not assessed as they are outside the assigned repository sources.

rejected_leads.lead: RegistryFileParser.getInstance() uses Class.forName(...,true,classLoader)/newInstance() on class names from a registry file (jt-utilities/.../RegistryFileParser.java:101-157).
rejected_leads.reason: The URL/class names come from classpath resources located by ConcurrentOperationRegistry; an attacker able to plant registry resources already controls the classpath, so this is not an independent vulnerability in this code.

Looks like a correctness bug (wrong accessor, possible NPE/exception for int tables), but no attacker-controlled path or meaningful confidentiality/integrity/availability impact could be shown; not a security finding at this evidence level.

rejected_leads.lead: Index 'sql' security_call hints in BufferOpImage/ZonalStatsOpImage (many spatialIndex.query() calls).
rejected_leads.reason: Verified these are JTS STRtree.query() spatial-index lookups, not SQL; name-based index hints are false positives.

Matches the standard Wirth quickselect pattern; no demonstrated out-of-bounds/infinite-loop condition from source review, and any failure would be a bounded exception/DoS rather than a strong security impact.
Variable names are prefixed with 'v_' and resolved against the runtime class itself; no arbitrary-field/class access beyond generated variables is shown.

rejected_leads.lead: Swing viewer/HTMLBuilder string rendering (jt-utilities/.../viewer/HTMLBuilder.java) and demo/Docs file I/O.
rejected_leads.reason: Local desktop viewer/demo code with no server-side untrusted input path; HTML output is not executed by a browser engine in the reviewed code.

summary: Repository: jai-ext (it.geosolutions.jaiext), ~490 files / 415 Java sources (image operators plus the Jiffle scripting/compiler module). Broad searches found no JDBC/XML/deserialization/process-exec/network sinks; the strongest evidence-backed issue is in the Jiffle script-to-Java compiler: raw attacker-supplied script text is embedded into the generated Java source inside a Javadoc block comment, and that source is then compiled by Janino and loaded/instantiated. The only sanitization, `stripComments`, removes `/* ... */` block comments but not `*/` sequences that survive elsewhere in a parseable script (e.g. inside a line comment), so a crafted script can terminate the generated comment and inject arbitrary Java declarations into the compiled runtime class. This is submitted as one candidate (code injection), with the key prerequisite (Jiffle line-comment syntax and consequent reachability of a `*/` that survives `stripComments`) not verifiable from the snapshot because the ANTLR grammar files are absent.
